neighbours.label: the word that closes a counted occasion or time offset: 'both times', 'each time', 'three days later'
fire: She applied for the grant twice and was turned down both times by the panel.
The dog ran off into the woods and, two days later, turned up at the farm.
He sat the exam in May and again in June and passed both times with ease.
The letter was posted on Monday and, a week later, it reached her desk.
The team met the champions twice last season and lost both times at home.
They planted the seeds in April and, six weeks later, the first shoots appeared.
The bill went to the senate twice and was blocked both times by one vote.
The climbers left the hut at midnight and, ten hours later, reached the summit.
quiet: She applied for the grant and was turned down by the panel.
The dog ran off into the woods and turned up at the farm.
He sat the exam in May and passed with ease.
The letter was posted on Monday and it reached her desk.
The team met the champions last season and lost at home.
They planted the seeds in April and the first shoots appeared.
The bill went to the senate and was blocked by one vote.
The climbers left the hut at midnight and reached the summit.

notes: Card: 'exonerated both [times]', 'for [each] variant', 'one of the two [copies]', 'three days [later]'; peak tokens ' each' x4, ' later' x4, ' time' x4, ' times' x3. Probe: 'three days later' 0.67, 'cleared both times' 0.51, 'for each variant' 0.17, 'two copies' 0.14, 'every time' 0.10, 'repeated four times' 0.04. So a bare count of repetitions is not enough; the strong cases pick out particular occasions. The - pole is the Python token ' return'.
